explanation: The plan flattened one square ad and cropped it twice, but the request required three genuinely rearranged layouts; cropping cannot reflow copy or reposition the cup. The catalogue’s misleading text warning also steered the agent toward a plain text-overlay tool that cannot deliver the requested typography and button styling.
better_chain: image (create a finished 1:1 campaign ad with a steaming cup, cream-and-dark-green palette, designed typography and all three exact phrases, using qwen-image-2.1) → image-edit (use the square ad as reference to create a genuinely rearranged 9:16 layout, preserving cup design, typography, palette and exact copy) → image-edit (use the same square reference to create a 16:9 layout with copy beside the cup rather than cropping the square) → check (inspect all three for exact wording, aspect ratios, campaign consistency and unclipped compositions; revise any failures)

steps.issue: Image generation is appropriate for creating the shared coffee visual, and the subject and palette are specified. A centrally composed source is usable as a reference, although it does not itself provide adapted layouts.

The plain text-overlay tool cannot design a coordinated headline, tagline and button around the cup. Asking for these through a single middle-positioned text band exceeds its capabilities; an image model should integrate the lettering into the ad design.
Cropping a finished square ad cannot rearrange its portrait layout. Using the flattened, already-lettered square also exposes the required copy to clipping rather than fitting it to the new canvas.
A landscape crop cannot reposition the cup and copy into a wide composition. It discards product content and produces another cropped copy rather than a genuinely adapted campaign variant.

missing: Separate layout adaptation for 9:16 and 16:9, plus final inspection of every variant for complete exact copy, intact product composition and consistent campaign styling.
